subject.title: Memory system: Cannot delete stale memories, conflicting entries persist

question: Should this concrete stale-memory report be fixed as a narrow LanceDB recall-to-forget handoff, or folded into the broader memory lifecycle contract in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/42650?
rationale: Source inspection proves a real deletion-handoff gap, but choosing UUID exposure, numeric selector state, text fallback, replacement, tombstone, or supersede behavior affects memory API and durable state semantics.

options.title: Define lifecycle contract first
options.body: Use the broader Memory MVP tracker to settle recall selectors, forget behavior, tombstones, superseded states, and conflict handling before implementation branches split apart.

options.title: Ship narrow LanceDB handoff
options.body: Expose deletable UUIDs in `memory_recall` content with focused regression coverage, while explicitly leaving replacement and conflict resolution to the broader tracker.

options.title: Defer to broad tracker only
options.body: Treat this issue as context for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/42650 and avoid a separate narrow LanceDB repair until the lifecycle API is chosen.

recommendation.title: Define lifecycle contract first
recommendation.body: Use the broader Memory MVP tracker to settle recall selectors, forget behavior, tombstones, superseded states, and conflict handling before implementation branches split apart.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory storage/schema work makes this the best available owner for durable lifecycle and plugin API direction.
